name.description: The name of the object being documented.

path.description:
The full path down to the object being documented.
This, in conjunction with the kind, should allow global resolution of the source object.

source.description:
The unparsed source of the documentation.  This comes from an annotation on the DSL, from
scripting language source code or from a separate DSL file.

description.description: The general description in the documentation, exclusive of block annotations such as `@param` and `@see`.

references.description: References to other pieces of documentation via `@see` annotations.

deprecated.description: Whether or not this structure is deprecated.

deprecateDetails.description: If deprecated, the reason and/or replacement.

deprecateFinalVersion.description: If deprecated, the final version supported.

beta.description: Whether or not this structure is a beta feature.

uses.description:
Other things which make use of this structure. For example, types that mix in the type being documented.
These are generated automatically from the metadata and are not present in the documentation comment itself.

pills.description:
Short labels which add extra info that can be flagged. These are typically displayed as oval "pills" of text
such as "required" and "abstract".

favorite.description: True if the user marked this element as a favorite, which makes it show up by default in some contexts.

examples.description: Extracted and/or synthesized example code, which should be directly usable for experimentation.

attributes.description:
The set of annotation attributes (name/value pairs).
The values are literals rendered as (abbreviated) text.

declaration.description: Markup of the annotation declaration formatted as a code span or pre block.

title: Documentation of a single annotation on a piece of metadata.
name: AnnotationDocumentation
